propositions.text: The Appellant, a citizen of El Salvador, appeals the RPD decision denying refugee protection.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXthe Appellant), a citizen of El Salvador, appeals a decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) denying his claim for refugee protection.

propositions.text: The Appellant submits new evidence and asks the RAD to accept it under Section 110(4) IRPA, set aside the Board's decision, and refer for a new hearing including 'inclusion' or an oral hearing under Section 110(6).
propositions.quote: He has submitted new evidence in support of his appeal. The Appellant asks the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to accept the new evidence in accordance to Section 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protections Act (IRPA), set aside the Board's decision and to refer the matter back to the RPD for a new hearing by a different member and to include the issue of "inclusion" in that hearing or to set an oral hearing in accordance to Section 110(6) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant appeals the RPD decision denying refugee protection and submits new evidence, requesting a new hearing or oral hearing under IRPA sections.

propositions.text: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(c) IRPA, the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1)(c) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA), the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: The court refers the matter back to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel under IRPA section 111(1)(c).

propositions.text: The Appellant alleged fear of the MS13 gang in El Salvador and the USA, fled El Salvador in 2000, held TPS in the USA, left again in 2008 due to threats, then came to Canada.
propositions.quote: The Appellant alleged before the RPD that he fears the gang known as the MS13, in El Salvador as well as in the U.S.A. Full details of his allegations are available in his Basis of Claim (BOC) narrative. The Appellant fled El Salvador in 2000, going to the U.S.A. where he held temporary protected status. He re-availed in 2008 and left again after learning the gang was still after him. He left the U.S.A. for Canada after receiving threatening phone calls there.

propositions.text: The Appellant crossed into Canada without reporting but was arrested later on an outstanding US warrant.
propositions.quote: He crossed into Canada without reporting to the Canada Border Services but was arrested sometime later on an outstanding U.S. warrant.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges fear of MS13 gang, fled El Salvador and USA, entered Canada irregularly, and was arrested on a US warrant, as reported to the RPD.

propositions.text: At the May 14, 2014 hearing, the only issue discussed was possible exclusion under Article 1F(b) of the Refugee Convention.
propositions.quote: The Appellant's application for refugee protection was brought before the Board for his hearing on May 14, 2014. During that hearing, the only issue discussed was in regards to the possible exclusion of the Appellant in accordance to Article 1F(b) of the 1951 Convention and the 1967 Protocol relating to the Status of Refugees (the Convention) which is articulated clearly in the United Nations High Commission for Refugees (UNHCR) handbook.

propositions.text: The RAD notes a detailed pre-hearing discussion among counsels and the Panel about facts, exclusion, witnesses, and law, some without the Appellant present.
propositions.quote: In listening to the audio tape, the RAD notes that there occurred a detailed pre-hearing discussion amongst the counsels for the Appellant, counsel for the Minister and the Panel regarding an agreed upon statement of facts, exclusion, whether to allow witness testimony on the exclusion, the law as it applies in Canada, the law as it was applied in XXXX and much more. Some of this discussion was had without the presence of the Appellant; however, the Appellant was present for much of it, including the portions of the hearing in which the issue of possible witnesses were discussed.

propositions.text: The Panel repeatedly stated there would be no re-trial of the conviction in XXXX during the hearing.
propositions.quote: The Panel made it clear on a number of occasions during this part of the hearing that there would be no re-trial of the conviction in XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker held a hearing focused on exclusion under Article 1F(b), with detailed pre-hearing discussions and no re-trial of the conviction.

propositions.text: The Panel requested written submissions on whether to consider potential defenses if charged in Canada, relating to Article 1F(b) exclusion.
propositions.quote: At the end of the morning, the Panel requested written submissions form both counsels in regards to one question to be considered by the Panel. The Panel asked "Should the Panel consider and take into account potential defenses which the claimant may have had and used, if he had been charged in Canada with the equivalent act?" This question was in relation to the Article 1F(b) exclusion.

propositions.text: The Panel and counsels agreed on submission dates and tentative plans for next steps after submissions and exclusion decision.
propositions.quote: The Panel and counsels agreed on dates for submissions and the Panel laid out tentative plans for what may occur once he had made his decision on the submissions and subsequently on the exclusion issue.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker requested written submissions on defenses relevant to exclusion and planned next steps with counsel agreement.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD erred by denying opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses, and make final presentations.
propositions.quote: a) The Appellant submits that the RPD erred by failing to allow the Appellant any opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses and to make final presentations.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD made factual findings without questioning witnesses.
propositions.quote: b) The Appellant submits that the RPD made numerous findings of fact without ever questioning the witness.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges denial of legal right to put his case forward.
propositions.quote: c) The Appellant submits that he was denied the legal right to put his case forward.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD recognized the matter was incomplete but issued decision anyway.
propositions.quote: d) The Appellant submits that the RPD recognized at the hearing that the matter was not yet completed but made and wrote its decision regardless of that recognition.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges breach of procedural fairness and legitimate expectations by denying right to testify.
propositions.quote: e) The Appellant submits that the RPD breached the Appellant's right to procedural fairness and violated the doctrine of legitimate expectations by denying him the right to testify.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD erred by referencing 'oral testimony' he never gave.
propositions.quote: f) The Appellant submits that the RPD made several errors in its decision by referencing to the Appellant's "oral testimony." The Appellant submits he never gave oral testimony.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges gross misrepresentations of his relationship and disapproval in the RPD decision.
propositions.quote: g) The Appellant submits that the RPD made gross misrepresentations of the Appellant and his common law spouse's relationship and the Panel's disapproval of the Appellant's actions is clearly obvious in his decision.

propositions.text: The Appellant alleges the RPD erred by failing to do a separate analysis under Section 97 IRPA.
propositions.quote: h) The Appellant submits that the RPD erred when it failed to do a separate analysis under Section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant alleges multiple errors by the RPD including denial of evidence presentation, procedural fairness breaches, factual errors, and failure to analyze under Section 97 IRPA.

propositions.text: The Appellant requests the RAD grant the appeal and refer for new hearing with different panel or order no exclusion and new inclusion hearing.
propositions.quote: The Appellant requests that the RAD grant this appeal and that it refer the matter back to the RPD for a new hearing with s different panel, or in the alternative, the Appellant asks the RAD to order that the Appellant is not excluded from refugee protection and a new hearing by the RPD be held on the inclusion case.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant requests the RAD grant the appeal and order a new hearing or no exclusion and new inclusion hearing.

propositions.text: Section 110(4) IRPA limits new evidence on appeal to evidence arising after rejection or not reasonably available before.
propositions.quote: Section 110(4) of the IRPA provides that the Appellant may present only evidence that arose after the rejection of his claim or that was not reasonably available, or that he could not reasonably have been expected in the circumstances to have presented, at the time of the rejection.

paragraphs.summary: Section 110(4) IRPA restricts new evidence on appeal to that arising after rejection or not reasonably available before, as stated by prior authority.

propositions.text: Even if evidence meets Section 110(4) test, RAD may still refuse admission; Appellant must fully submit how evidence meets requirements and relates to him.
propositions.quote: Even where a document meets the test in Section 110(4), this does not require the RAD to admit it into evidence without any further consideration. It is for the Appellant to make full and detailed submissions in his Memorandum about how any proposed new evidence meets the requirements of Section 110(4) and how that evidence relates to the Appellant.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD may refuse evidence despite meeting Section 110(4); Appellant must fully submit how evidence qualifies and relates to him.

propositions.text: In Raza, FCA held 'newness' of evidence depends on event proved, not just document creation date.
propositions.quote: In Raza, paragraph 16, the Federal Court of Appeal endorsed the principle that a document's "newness" cannot be tested solely by its date of creation; what is important is the event or circumstance sought to be proved by the evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Raza that 'newness' of evidence depends on the event proved, not just document date.

propositions.text: Two affidavits disclosed in Appellant's record lack mention under RAD Rule 29 or in Memorandum, but RAD will consider them for fairness under Section 110(4).
propositions.quote: In regards to this appeal, two affidavits were disclosed in the Appellant's record which the RAD can find no mention of in regards to Rule 29 of the RAD rules. Further, there is no mention of these affidavits in the Memorandum, either. However, in an effort to be as fair as possible, the RAD will look at these and make a decision on their admissibility in accordance to Section 110(4) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes two affidavits lack procedural mention but will consider them fairly under Section 110(4) IRPA.

propositions.text: First affidavit from Ms. XXXX, a lawyer, attests to hearing the May 16, 2014 hearing recording and confirms Panel's statements about decision communication and hearing status.
propositions.quote: The first affidavit is one from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a lawyer at the law office of XXXX XXXX (counsel of record for the Appellant). In this affidavit, Ms. XXXX attests to the facts regarding the hearing of May 16, 2014 including, after she listened to the official recording of that proceeding, an exchange in which the Panel confirmed that he would communicate in writing his decision on whether he will allow testimony from the family members. Further, she attests to the point that at no point in the recording does the panel state that the hearing was completed and that he would be making his final decision.

paragraphs.summary: The first affidavit from a lawyer attests to the May 16, 2014 hearing recording and Panel's statements about decision communication and hearing status.

propositions.text: The first affidavit is not new as it only reiterates the official hearing record and is not material; it will be disallowed.
propositions.quote: Is this affidavit "new"? The RAD finds that it is not new, as it deals only with the recorded record of the hearing which occurred on May 16, 2014. There is nothing new in the affidavit and the content of the affidavit itself is not material because it only reiterates what was on the official record. This affidavit will be disallowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the first affidavit not new and disallows it as it only repeats the official hearing record.

propositions.text: Second affidavit from Ms. XXXX attests to conversations she heard secondhand between Ms. XXXX and Minister's counsel Mr. Klaus.
propositions.quote: The second affidavit comes from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, also a lawyer at Ms. XXXX firm. In this affidavit, Ms. XXXX attests to the content of conversations between Ms. XXXX and the counsel for the Minister, Mr. Klaus. Ms. XXXX heard none of the conversations related to in the affidavit but is only attesting to what she was told afterwards by Ms. XXXX.

paragraphs.summary: The second affidavit attests to secondhand conversations between counsel, as described by a lawyer.

propositions.text: The second affidavit is new and relates to post-hearing conversations; it is allowed and considered despite hearsay nature.
propositions.quote: The document is new and does speak to conversations which occurred after the hearing so in that regard, it may be considered under Section 110(4) as allowable. Even though the RAD can give less weight to such hearsay evidence, the affidavit will be allowed and considered by the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the second affidavit new and allows it despite hearsay, as it concerns post-hearing conversations.

propositions.text: Counsel made submissions on the RAD's role in reviewing RPD decisions.
propositions.quote: Counsel has made some submissions in regard to the role that the RAD plays in the review of an RPD decision.

propositions.text: The Federal Court decision in Huruglica guides that RAD conducts a hybrid appeal, independently assessing RPD decisions and substituting its own decision if differing.
propositions.quote: However, the RAD finds that the recent Federal Court decision, in Huruglica,3 provides the RAD with guidance in relation to the appropriate standard that must be applied by a specialized tribunal such as the RAD to decisions of a first-level administrative tribunal. Justice Phelan states in paragraphs 54 and 55 of the foregoing decision: [54] Having concluded that the RAD erred in reviewing the RPD's decision on the standard of reasonableness, I have further concluded that for the reasons above, the RAD is required to conduct a hybrid appeal. It must review all aspects of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the claimant is a Convention refugee or a person in need of protection. Where its assessment departs from that of the RPD, the RAD must substitute its own decision. [55] In conducting its assessment, it can recognize and respect the conclusion of the RPD on such issues as credibility and/or where the RPD enjoys a particular advantage in reaching such a conclusion but it is not restricted, as an appellate court is, to intervening on facts only where there is an "overriding and palpable error."

paragraphs.summary: Counsel submitted on RAD's role; the court cites Huruglica that RAD conducts a hybrid appeal with independent assessment and substitution of decision if differing.

propositions.text: The RAD will independently assess the RPD's decision and decide if the Appellant should be excluded under Article 1F(b).
propositions.quote: Accordingly, the RAD will conduct its own assessment of the RPD's decision and come to an independent assessment of whether the Appellant should be excluded in accordance to Article 1F(b).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the RAD will independently assess the RPD decision on exclusion under Article 1F(b).

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD erred by denying opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses, and make final presentations.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD erred by failing to allow the Appellant any opportunity to present evidence, question witnesses and to make final presentations.

propositions.text: The RPD was required to consider the Minister's exclusion request before any inclusion hearing.
propositions.quote: The RPD was required to look at the Minister's request for exclusion before any hearing of inclusion could occur.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues RPD denied procedural rights; the court notes RPD had to consider exclusion before inclusion hearing.

propositions.text: Section 101(1) IRPA lists grounds making a claim ineligible for RPD referral, including prior refugee protection, rejected claims, inadmissibility, etc.
propositions.quote: 101. (1) A claim is ineligible to be referred to the Refugee Protection Division if a) refugee protection has been conferred on the claimant under this Act; b) a claim for refugee protection by the claimant has been rejected by the Board; c) a prior claim by the claimant was determined to be ineligible to be referred to the Refugee Protection Division, or to have been withdrawn or abandoned; d) the claimant has been recognized as a Convention refugee by a country other than Canada and can be sent or returned to that country; e) the claimant came directly or indirectly to Canada from a country designated by the regulations, other than a country of their nationality or their former habitual residence; or f) the claimant has been determined to be inadmissible on grounds of security, violating human or international rights, serious criminality or organized criminality, except for persons who are inadmissible solely on the grounds of paragraph 35(1)(c). (2) A claim is not ineligible by reason of serious criminality under paragraph (1)(f) unless a) in the case of inadmissibility by reason of a conviction in Canada, the conviction is for an offence under an Act of Parliament punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least 10 years; or b) in the case of inadmissibility by reason of a conviction outside Canada, the conviction is for an offence that, if committed in Canada, would constitute an offence under an Act of Parliament punishable by a maximum term of imprisonment of at least 10 years.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Section 101(1) IRPA listing grounds for claim ineligibility for RPD referral, including prior protection, rejected claims, inadmissibility.

propositions.text: The Appellant pleaded guilty in XXXX court to Sexual Assault 4th Degree with specified elements.
propositions.quote: In this particular appeal, the facts are laid out before the RAD as follows: 1) The Appellant pleaded guilty in an XXXX court to "Sexual Assault 4th Degree".4 The elements of such a charge and this one in particular are that a) the accused is twenty years of age or older, b) the accused engaged in sexual intercourse with a person who is c) less than 16 years of age and d) who is not the person's spouse.

propositions.text: The Appellant pled guilty based on those elements.
propositions.quote: 2) The Appellant pled guilty to this offense based on those elements listed above.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Appellant pleaded guilty to Sexual Assault 4th Degree with specified elements in XXXX court.

propositions.text: The Appellant pleaded guilty to sexual intercourse with a person under 16 who was not his spouse, while he was over 20.
propositions.quote: the Appellant pleaded guilty to having sexual intercourse with a person under the age of 16 who was not the Appellant's spouse, while he was over the age of 20.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the Appellant pleaded guilty to sexual intercourse with a person under 16 who was not his spouse.

propositions.text: The RAD must consider if the conviction would be treated differently in Canada.
propositions.quote: What the RAD must consider now is whether or not the conviction in XXXX would be treated differently in Canada.

propositions.text: Counsel argues no charges would be laid in Canada as the victim was actually the Appellant's spouse.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the Appellant argues that in Canada, there would not even be any charges laid as the so-called victim was in fact the Appellant's spouse.

propositions.text: The Minister argued the plea bargain acknowledges the victim was not the spouse at the time of assault and conviction.
propositions.quote: The Minister argued at the RPD that the plea bargain agreed to by the Appellant in XXXX acknowledges on his part that the "victim" was not his spouse at the time of the assault and at the time of the conviction

propositions.text: The RAD recognizes the Appellant disagrees with calling the female a victim.
propositions.quote: the RAD recognizes that the Appellant disagrees with referring to the female in question as a victim

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must decide if the conviction would be treated differently in Canada; the Appellant's counsel argues no charges as the victim was spouse; the Minister says plea acknowledges victim was not spouse; the RAD notes Appellant disagrees with calling her a victim.

propositions.text: The Appellant argues the RPD breached natural justice by denying him opportunity to testify, have witnesses heard, and present evidence.
propositions.quote: The Appellant argues that the RPD breached natural justice when it failed to allow the Appellant an opportunity to testify, to have witnesses heard and to present evidence in support of his case.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant argues the RPD breached natural justice by denying him testimony, witnesses, and evidence presentation.

propositions.text: The RAD has considered the natural justice issue and the doctrine of legitimate expectations carefully.
propositions.quote: The RAD has considered this carefully and has also considered the "doctrine of legitimate expectations." Natural Justice

paragraphs.summary: The RAD has carefully considered natural justice and the doctrine of legitimate expectations.

propositions.text: The only issue now is natural justice regarding the exclusion clause interpretation.
propositions.quote: The only issue that the RAD needs to deal with at this point is the issue of natural justice.

propositions.text: Interpretation of exclusion clause requires evaluating crime elements, prosecution mode, penalty, facts, and circumstances of conviction.
propositions.quote: the interpretation of the exclusion clause in Article 1F(b) of the Convention, as regards the seriousness of a crime, requires an evaluation of the elements of the crime, the mode of prosecution, the penalty prescribed, the facts and the mitigating and aggravating circumstances underlying the conviction

propositions.text: Presumption of seriousness may be rebutted by crime elements and circumstances but not by extraneous factors like persecution risk.
propositions.quote: There is no balancing, however, with factors extraneous to the facts and circumstances underlying the conviction such as, for example, the risk of persecution in the state of origin

paragraphs.summary: The RAD states the issue is natural justice; prior authority requires evaluating crime elements and circumstances, excluding extraneous factors like persecution risk.

propositions.text: The RPD must allow the Appellant and witnesses to testify to properly evaluate the crime elements.
propositions.quote: this requirement to evaluate the elements of the crime, etc., requires the RPD to allow the Appellant to testify to and have witnesses testify to the elements of the crime.

propositions.text: No proper evaluation can be made without hearing from the Appellant and his witnesses.
propositions.quote: No proper and complete evaluation can be made without hearing from the Appellant and his witnesses.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD must allow the Appellant and witnesses to testify for a proper evaluation of the crime elements.

propositions.text: The RAD listened to the May 16, 2014 hearing recording and found the Appellant's testimony and right to final submissions were omitted.
propositions.quote: The RAD has listened to the recording of the hearing of May 16, 2014... the two things that were left out of the hearing was the Appellant's testimony and the Appellant's right to make final submissions on the exclusion.

propositions.text: The Panel did not allow testimony and ended suggesting later submissions, but no further hearing occurred before decision.
propositions.quote: The Panel clearly did not allow testimony at the hearing... A tentative hearing date was set but... before the next hearing date could be set, the Panel reached his decision on exclusion and rendered it in writing

propositions.text: The Appellant was excluded without ever being allowed to speak at his exclusion hearing.
propositions.quote: excluding him without ever allowing the Appellant to speak to his own exclusion hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the May 16, 2014 hearing omitted the Appellant's testimony and final submissions; no further hearing occurred before exclusion decision.

propositions.text: Counsel argues the Panel disallowed testimony despite Appellant's request, which was an error.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the Appellant argues that the Panel disallowed testimony at the hearing despite the Appellant's request. This refusal was an error on the part of the Panel.

propositions.text: By refusing testimony and arguments, the RPD breached natural justice and the decision cannot stand.
propositions.quote: By refusing to allow the Appellant to present arguments and testimony at the hearing on exclusion, the RPD did breach natural justice and for that reason, the decision cannot stand.

paragraphs.summary: The Appellant's counsel argues refusal of testimony was error; the RAD finds RPD breached natural justice and decision cannot stand.

propositions.text: The RAD found the RPD breached natural justice by denying testimony, witnesses, and final submissions on exclusion.
propositions.quote: The RAD has found that the RPD did breach natural justice by not allowing the Appellant to testify or to have witnesses heard or to make final submissions at the hearing of his exclusion issue.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD found the RPD breached natural justice by denying the Appellant testimony, witnesses, and final submissions.

propositions.text: Pursuant to IRPA s.111(1)(c), the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to Section 111(1) (c) of IRPA, the RAD refers the matter to the RPD for re-determination by a differently-constituted panel.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD orders referral to the RPD for re-determination by a different panel under IRPA s.111(1)(c).
